findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', at both widths
findings.fault: The article title is set in a heavy bold Gelasio. It is clearly darker and blunter than anything else on the page, the subhead below it included. The tile's own type-pair panel says article titles are SemiBold, and the rest of the type is regular or semibold. Against the light, refined large line on the first screen, the article page opens with a slab of black type that looks like a newspaper headline.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for 'refined, never childish' and serious type, would see the article page as heavier than the homepage. Angélique, who builds new articles from the stated spec ('SemiBold for article titles'), would get a title that doesn't match what the page shows.

findings.where: Article specimen, the apostrophe in the title 'World's', against the curly quotes in the subhead ('‘chapter topics’') and body (“…”)
findings.fault: The title's apostrophe is a straight typewriter mark, which looks like a tapered tick in bold Gelasio. Every other quote in the article is a curly typographer's quote. The one typewriter mark sits in the largest type of the article.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader at a development bank, used to well-set legal and policy papers, would notice the mismatch in the title and read it as a lapse of care, on a page meant to show Mark's work as carefully made.

findings.where: First screen at phone width, the row of topic labels under the lead (PPP Law · Infrastructure · Development banks / · Governments · Risk allocation)
findings.fault: When the labels wrap, the second line starts with a middle-dot separator ('· Governments'). The dot hangs at the left edge like a list bullet, and the line does not align with the label above it.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor sees a stray bullet starting the second line. It reads as a broken list rather than one row of labels, and spoils an otherwise clean left edge in the hero.

findings.where: Below the fold, the section heads: 'Palette', 'Texture', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' compared with 'Motion sketch' and the line 'placed, calm, exact' under it
findings.fault: Every specimen section is headed by a small SemiBold sans label, except the motion sketch. It adds a second, large lowercase sans heading ('placed, calm, exact') in a size and style used nowhere else. Like parts are treated unlike, and this extra display line in the sans goes against the tile's own rule that the large display role belongs to Gelasio.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing tiles section by section, would see one section styled differently from its siblings with no reason given. The lowercase large sans line also reads as a slogan in a different voice from Mark's serif.
